walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme A: Relationships & Families — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme A: Relationships & Families brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme A: Relationships & Families.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which encyclical banned Catholic contraception in 1968?
options: Humanae Vitae
Rerum Novarum
Pacem in Terris
Laudato Si

mcqs.q: What is the maximum number of wives in Islam?
What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.
Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
